concerns.text: The plan states it will “run paired McNemar’s test (`statsmodels.stats.contingency_tables.mcnemar`). If any cell = 0, switch to exact McNemar’s (`scipy.stats.binom_test`).” However, the aggregation step (2.1) collapses the data to total counts per vulnerability type (human_count, llm_count) and loses the per‑pair information required for a true paired McNemar test. McNemar’s test assumes a 2×2 contingency table of discordant outcomes for the same subjects (e.g., for each code pair: vulnerability present in human, present in LLM). Using aggregated counts treats the groups as independent samples, which violates the test’s assumptions and can yield misleading significance results. This constitutes a methodological flaw rather than a circular validation.
